memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"During the last watch of the night the LORD looked down from the pillar of fire
and cloud at the Egyptian army and threw it into confusion. He jammed the wheels
of their chariots so that they had difficulty driving. And the Egyptians said,
'Let's get away from the Israelites! The LORD is fighting for them against
Egypt.'" - Ex 14:24-25 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God looks down, and an army falls apart.

He does not need to send lightning. He looks, and there is confusion. He jams
the wheels of the most advanced military machines of the ancient world.

There is something almost understated about this. The chariots, Egypt's pride,
become useless. The thing they trusted becomes the thing that traps them in the
sea bed.

Then the Egyptians say something remarkable: "The LORD is fighting for them."
The enemy speaks the truth of verse 14 back to us. They have finally understood
who they are dealing with, though too late to change course.

Notice the timing: "the last watch of the night." Just before dawn. The darkest,
coldest, longest part of the night, when Israel had been walking for hours and
must have wondered if they would make it.

God's help often arrives near dawn. Not because He is slow, but because He is
precise. Psalm 46:5 says God helps "at break of day."

If you are in the last watch, hold on. That is not the same as being abandoned.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What are you trusting that could become the very thing that traps you?
2. Are you in a "last watch" season, waiting for light?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, You need only look and my enemies scatter. Help me through the last
watch of this night and let me see Your morning. Amen.
